blocks.x: Introduction to Organization’s Project Quality Plan

r.x: This project quality plan is in line with the organisation's Quality Management System (ISO 9001: 2015 QMS requirements) and Information Security Management System (ISO/IEC 27001:2022 ISMS requirements) designed to ensure consistent working practices adhering to all applicable legal and contractual requirements, in delivering our services to our clients, vendors and shareholders thereby ensuring complete satisfaction at all levels through continual improvement and preserving Confidentiality (C), Integrity (I) and Availability (A) of information.
The Quality Plan defines the Operating Procedures to be followed during the project execution. This document comprises of a minimum of the following.
Project Organization Structure
Operating Procedures
Applicable Documents
Inspection & Test Plan (Will be included in the respective method statements)
Work Method Statements (Method statements will be submitted separately for Engineer’s approval)

The Project Manager in co-ordination with relevant functions Technical Director, Procurement Manager, Contracts Manager, Planning Manager, Construction Managers, Commissioning Manager and Commercial Manager identifies the opportunities and risks associated with the various stages of the project i.e. Design, Procurement, Contracts, Planning, Construction, Commissioning and Commercial. The same team led by Project Manager ensures appropriate strategies / control measures are in place to mitigate the risk / achieve the identified opportunity during the project life.
The Opportunities, Risks and the appropriate measures to address them, the progress of accomplishing those measures are managed using Opportunities & Risk Register
{{CO}} appointed specialist subcontractors will be advised to submit the risks and appropriate mitigation measures pertaining to their scope.
The Project Manager and the key functions as referred above will monitor the implementation of mitigation measures.

The Opportunities & Risk Register is a live document and shall be updated as and when a new risk / opportunity is identified during the course of the project or to reflect the progress of proposed actions and the corresponding reduction of risk rating.
The Project Manager and the Planning Manager jointly review the project program and notify the client officially through the MC, of any discrepancy.

The Project Manager submits the MEP work program for incorporation into the overall Main Contractor’s Program.
The complete Project Program, once approved by the Engineer, will then be issued by MC to {{CO}}.
The Project Manager distributes the approved Work Program to the site team including Subcontractors, for implementation and progress update.

The Project Planning Engineer in co-ordination with the Project Manager or his delegates prepare look ahead program based on the look ahead program issued by the MC, to have a better control of the project milestones and monitor the project progress accordingly.
The look ahead program will be the basis of short term resource planning.
The Project Manager issues contractual notices for any delay to the approved work program as necessary.
Actual access dates shall be submitted to the MC as part of regular reports.
The Project Planning Engineer in co-ordination with the Project Manager prepares the manpower histogram based on the approved work program and monitors the same on a regular basis.
The Planner updates the progress of the work and submits reports to MC based on the contract requirements, in co-ordination with the Project Manager.

The project dash boards and KPIs are defined in co-ordination with MC and monitored to ensure continual improvement. Where KPI’s could not be met, appropriate measures are taken to mitigate the delays.

blocks.x: Inspection and Test Plan / Method Statements

r.x: The QCE in co-ordination with respective RDE develops Inspection & Test Plan based on the contract requirements, scope of work, detailing the inspection process such as the activity to be inspected, hold points, witness, test and approvals and submits to MC for approval.
The Method statements and ITPs are reviewed by the RDE and approved by the Project Manager prior to submission to the consultant for approval.
Upon consultant’s approval, the ITP will be circulated/briefed to the project team including the Subcontractors, as applicable.

The QCE prepares the method statements in co-ordination with respective RDE/CM based on the contract requirements, scope of work and submit to MC for approval prior to the start of the particular installation at site.
The HSE Officer and the respective Discipline Engineer assess the risks pertaining to a particular installation and is included in the Method Statement.
The method statements and risk assessments are submitted for Consultant’s approval.
The submission and approval of Method Statements are logged and monitored using Method Statement Register.

The Consultant approved method statements and risk assessments are addressed to the workforce prior to the start of installation / testing activities. Where there are changes in the methodology or in the work environment, the subject method statement shall be revised together with the risk assessment.

The tender drawings, specifications, value engineering proposals, BOQ are suitably identified and recorded as per Project File Index superseding previous revisions and all related drawings as applicable are controlled using Drawing Register.
The Technical Director in co-ordination with the PD develops the Drawing Register to suit the program.
{{CO}} Design Engineer ensures that all designs are in line with design approvals issued by MC and proceeds with Design drawing development.
Discrepancies between end design and authority design approval forwarded to {{CO}} will be raised as an issue and cleared (variation / design approval....) prior to proceeding.
RFIs are raised as applicable for clarifying unclear or ambiguous area.
The Drawing Flow Sheet (
OPEM-SD-Log
) is maintained to monitor and track the progress of shop drawing submissions and approvals.
All drawings generated shall complete an internal review procedure.
On successful completion of the internal review process, the Head Office DC uploads the drawing through mail to main contractor to get the Consultants approval.

Upon receipt of the approved drawings from the Consultant, the respective discipline Engineer as applicable (based on the scope) ensures the drawing issuance to the site duly signed and stamped as ‘ISSUED FOR CONSTRUCTION’.
The Drawing Flow Sheet (OPEM-SD-Log) is updated to reflect the above developments.

The discipline Engineer / QCE at site ensures that the drawings available with the Foremen / Subcontractors/ Specialists are of the latest revision and previous revisions are retrieved/stamped and segregated separately as ‘SUPERSEDED’.

On completion of the Inspection process pertaining to a specific Installation, the discipline Engineers ensure that the redline (mark-up) drawings are generated and submitted to the site office for developing the As Built Drawing.

The project QCE and the discipline Engineer checks the accuracy of redline (mark-up) drawings; where required spot checks are conducted, and the drawings are signed by the discipline Engineer to authenticate the accuracy of the mark-up drawings.
The Redline mark-up drawings authorised by the discipline Engineer are maintained in the server as per the Project File Index.

Drawing Flow Sheet	(OPEM-SD-Log)

Assessment of Vendors / Subcontractors
The Procurement Department maintains a list of Approved vendors / Subcontractors based on company’s Vendor / Subcontractor / Specialist Evaluation Procedure.
The List of approved vendors / subcontractors / specialists reflect the grade of the vendor/subcontractor/specialist based on their performance in the previous projects of {{CO}}.
The following grading system has been defined for the classification of vendors/subcontractors based on their performance.
A. Rated between 80 to 100
B. Rated between 60 to 79
C. Rated between 50 to 59
D. Rated between 36 to 49
E. Rated between 0 to 35

Any new Vendor / Subcontractor / Specialist being considered will undergo assessment based on the Vendor / Subcontractor Evaluation Procedure; only those which undergo successful assessment process will be considered to work with {{CO}}.
Procurement Procedure
The PD and the discipline Engineers review the project specification and the technical details.

The PD in co-ordination with the Planning Manager, Technical Director / Design Manager and Procurement Manager prepares the Material flow sheet identifying the planned submission dates of the material submittals, approval required dates, order placement dates, required delivery dates on site etc. and agrees with procurement department for their information and action.

The assigned Lead Engineers (DE for Main Equipment and Project Engineer for running items) prepare the material schedules complete with quantity take offs and forward them with Material Requisition for Enquiry purpose to Procurement, to obtain offers from Suppliers.

The Procurement Department floats enquiries, inviting proposals from the vendors considered during tendering stage and new vendors listed as approved by {{CO}}. If Confidentiality / Non-Disclosure agreements is a requirement as per the contract, the procurement team shall ensure that the NDA is executed prior to forwarding the project details to the Supplier.
On receipt of bids / offers, the PRM / PRE conducts a preliminary review and the copy of the technical offers are forwarded to the designated Lead Engineers for technical review.
The assigned Lead Engineers review the offers ensuring compliance with the specification, local authorities and with the project requirements.
All comments along with recommendation if any, are sent to the procurement department for further negotiations with the suppliers.
The PRM / PRE prepares Price Comparison Sheet taking into account the technical / commercial aspects and submit for the approval of authorised signatory.
If required, PRM issues a conditional LOI to the selected supplier, signed by the authorised signatory (CEO/COO), locking the prices, payment terms, special conditions and agreements.
The PRM ensures that the supplier acknowledges LOIs before commencing with the submission of material submittals.

The PRM co-ordinates with the suppliers to obtain the technical and sample material submittals, reviews the submittals and ensures that all submittals include compliance statement clearly indicating deviations from the specification if any, stamped with the supplier’s company stamp.

The material submittals are reviewed in accordance with technical submittal review procedure. The technical submittal review is documented using Technical Submittal Review Sign off Sheets. Technical Submittal Review Sign off Sheet for Main Equipment and Technical Submittal Review Sign off Sheet for Running Items).
The HO - DC uploads the submittals in mail for Main contractor / Consultant’s approval.
The As submitted copy is maintained in the server as per the Project File Index
The DC updates the Material Submittal Register (
OPEM-MS-Log

Upon receipt of the approved material submittal, the assigned Lead Engineer (DE for Main Equipment and PE for Running items) initiates the Material Requisition (MR) for purchase with detailed description and appropriate cost codes, obtains the signatures of PM and forwards to the Central Stores and Procurement department.
The As submitted copy of Material Requisition to be issued to the storekeeper for reference.
All Material Requisitions for Purchase should be attached with the following.
Copy of Consultant’s approval
Copy of technical specification where required
Delivery Schedule
Variation notification from {{CO}}, variation approval / approved instruction from the MC (for variation works) if applicable.
Request for Air Freight, substantiating detrimental impact on the project, if the items are not air freighted.

The Procurement department prepares the LPO, obtains the necessary approvals as per the company’s authority limits and forwards to the supplier. A copy of the LPO (without price) is forwarded to the project site office for record purpose.
Applicable Forms
Material Submittal Register	(OPEM-MS-Log)
Appointment of Subcontractor

The assigned Lead Engineer initiates the Subcontractor / Specialist Requisition attached with the package details, scope matrix, specification, contract BOQ / actual BOQ (for re-measured contract), drawing etc., obtains the approval of Project Manager and forward to Procurement.

The Procurement Department floats invitation to tender / price with all the details to a minimum of three companies. If Confidentiality / Non-Disclosure agreements is a requirement as per the contract, the procurement team shall ensure that the NDA is executed prior to forwarding the project details to the Subcontractor.
The Request For Quotation issued to the subcontractor shall comprise of a minimum of the following:
Detailed scope of works
Complete List of Drawings
Technical Specifications (as applicable)
Approved Material Submittals ( as applicable)
General Terms and Conditions
Responsibility Matrix
Form for submitting Subcontractors’ / Specialists quotation
On receipt of price bids / offer, the PRM/PRE conducts a preliminary review, and the copy of the technical offers are forwarded to the designated Lead Engineers for technical review.

The assigned Lead Engineers review the offers ensuring compliance with the specification, local authorities and with the project requirements, where found necessary conducts 2nd party audit of the Subcontractor’s QA system or project visits in co-ordination with QA team.
All comments along with recommendation if any, are sent to the procurement department for further negotiations with the subcontractor.

The PRM / PRE prepares the price comparison sheet highlighting the selected Subcontractor, taking into account the technical / commercial aspects and obtains the approval of Project Manager, Cost Control Manager, Procurement Manager and COO / CEO as applicable as per the authority limits.

The PRM ensures that the Subcontractor acknowledges the LOI.
The Subcontractor will be advised to provide the material submittal for onward submission to consultant for approval, where applicable.
On approval of the submittal, the PRM issues the Subcontract Agreement to the Subcontractor, which replaces the Letter of Intent.

The respective Design Engineer to identify the FAT requirements from the specification/tender clarification/value engineering and/or from all applicable documents and summarises the FAT requirements using FAT requirements in co-ordination with the procurement Engineer.
The FAT requirements are forwarded to QCE to develop a FAT schedule in coordination with the project team, MC and client.
The QCE prepares and submit the relevant FAT procedure and method statement to MC and consultant for approval and proceed with Factory visits as per agreed schedule with all stakeholders.

On successful completion of FAT, the related test reports are signed off by all parties and the same is forwarded to all parties for their records. The FAT report is saved in the server as per Project File Index.

The respective Construction Manager / Discipline Engineer /Foremen is responsible to verify the stock records pertaining to his discipline to ensure the availability of the required materials as per the Look Ahead Plan.
The material delivered from the supplier / subcontractor shall be handled as below:
Upon delivery of the material ordered by {{CO}} to the site, the Site Storekeeper arranges to unload the materials in the identified quarantine area.

For the materials delivered by the subcontractors, the subcontractor’s Store Keeper receives the materials, signs and stamps the receipt on the Delivery Order and submit to {{CO}} Storekeeper for signature.
The SSK receives the materials from the supplier, checks the quantity as per the delivery note/order, checks for damages if any and if found satisfactory, stamps the delivery note as
‘GOODS RECEIVED SUBJECT TO QUALITY CHECKS’
and stores materials safely.

The SSK notifies the RDE /QCE at site of the material receipt to conduct internal inspection. For Subcontractors’ materials the subcontractor should submit the Delivery Order duly signed by the {{CO}} Store Keeper to QCE.
The RDE / QCE inspects the delivered materials based on the approved material submittals and technical requirements.

If found satisfactory, the Site Storekeeper stores the material in the designated area with appropriate tagging and suitable identification. If the delivered material is not in line with the requirements, the discipline Engineer in co-ordination with the Storekeeper ensures suitable action.
The Storekeeper should ensure that the materials are stored as per the manufacturers’ recommendations.
The store keeper records the receipts of material in the Inventory Database.
Materials are issued to the site based on the Stores Issue Voucher (OXYPRO-MC-FM-04) initiated by the Foreman, approved by the respective Discipline Engineer.
All issuance of materials are recorded in the Inventory Database.
Site to site material transfers (permanent) are recorded using Material Transfer Voucher and temporary transfers are documented using Delivery Note
Material return to the suppliers in case of rejections should be documented using Delivery Note
Upon issuance of the materials from the storage area, the Site foreman ensures that materials are handled in a proper and safe manner.
Any damage to the material released from site stores for construction purpose, the respective foreman will be held responsible.

The SSK maintains and updates the Equipment Register to monitor the equipment available at site, their location, the condition of the equipment (working condition / under repair); the calibration status of measuring instruments.

The SSK closely monitors the calibration due dates of measuring instruments, ensures all measuring instruments are calibrated on a timely manner and the latest calibration certificates are made available in the server as per the Project File Index
The Site Storekeeper logs and tracks the movement of the Equipment and Tools available at site using Equipment’s / Tools Issue Register.
The Site Safety Officer in co-ordination with the respective foreman ensures that the power tools are inspected prior to the release to the site and are free from hazards.
All flammable and damaged materials are to be stored in a suitably defined and isolated area. Appropriate warning signs and symbols are to be provided at designated areas.
The SSK in co-ordination with the HSE Officer, discipline CM/PE ensures that the scrap generated is segregated at designated area as per main contractor’s waste management procedure.

The HSE Officer to study the risks / hazards with respect to the nature of scrap, the SSK arranges inspection by respective RDE / SM followed by the disposal of scrap as per {{CO}} scrap disposal procedure.
Material procured by {{CO}}

On receipt of the material delivery notification from the site store keeper, the QCE / RDE internally inspect the delivered materials based on the approved material submittals and review the material test certificates. MIR to be raised with all the attached documents, e.g. Test Certificates, Certificate of Country of Origin, Bill of Lading certificates, etc., as applicable.

If the material is found acceptable, the QA/QC Engineer initiates Material Inspection Request (as per the format provided by MC) attached with applicable documents like Test Certificates, Certificate of Country of Origin, Bill of lading etc. for approval and liaises with the Consultant to obtain approval.
The MC uploads the Material Inspection Request Status in mail. {{CO}} DC Logs and monitors the approval status of the Material Inspection Request using Material Inspection Request Register.

If the materials are not acceptable, the QCE notifies the RDE for taking necessary corrections in co-ordination with the PRM. Material Receipt Voucher will not be generated and forwarded to HO unless the material is replaced and the matter is rectified with the supplier.

For those materials which cannot be returned, they are clearly marked and segregated to prevent inadvertent use. The PD in co-ordination with Director of Projects & Procurement Manager will determine the relevant method of disposal. (E.g. scrap, return to supplier, and sell in concession or alternate usage).
Once the delivered material has been inspected and approved on site, it is used for installation and testing purposes.
Material Procured by {{CO}} appointed Subcontractors
The subcontractor’s material delivered at site must undergo the below inspections:
Internal Inspection by {{CO}}.
External Inspection by the consultant through {{CO}}.

The subcontractor must submit the copy of the supplier’s delivery order, attached with all applicable documents like Country of Origin, Test Certificates etc. duly signed and stamped the receipt by the subbie’s representative to {{CO}} Storekeeper on the same day the material has been received at site.

The storekeeper signs the DO with the date of receipt and distribute the DO to the QA/QC Engineers, discipline Engineer, CM, PD and the subcontractor. [*For specialised systems like BMS, FM-200 system, etc., the DO must be distributed to both Electrical and Mechanical Project Engineers and QA/QC Engineers at site]
The QA/QC Engineer checks the DO and the material against approved technical submittal.

If the material does not comply with the approved technical submittal, the QA/QC Engineer must ‘REJECT’ the material and the matter must be brought to the attention of the discipline Engineer and the subcontractor where applicable, for suitable rectification measures.
The QA/QC Engineer must not submit the Material Inspection Request to the consultant, until the issues are resolved.

Installation will not be permitted until the subcontractor delivers the correct material in line with the approved material submittal and the Material Inspection Request is approved by the Consultant.
If the material complies with the approved material submittal, the QA/QC Engineer submits Material Inspection Request to the consultant attaching a minimum of the following:
Delivery Order duly signed and stamped by subcontractor’s representative and {{CO}} storekeeper.
Cover sheet of the approved material submittal.
Country of origin, Test Certificates where applicable.
On receiving the commented MIR, the QA/QC Engineer reviews the comments.

If MIR not approved, the subcontractor will be advised to take appropriate action; following the verification, the QA/QC Engineer will revise and resubmit the Material Inspection Request and wait for the Consultant’s approval.
*Note: The subcontractor must not install the subject material until the revised Material Inspection Request is approved by the Consultant.
If MIR approved, the DC stamps the DO with the MIR Reference, Date, and status and forwards the DO to the subcontractor.

{{CO}} will certify Monthly Payment Applications if and only if the Payment Applications are attached with the DO copies stamped with the approved MIR Reference, Date of Inspections and the approval status of the material inspection request.

blocks.x: Control of Inspection, Measuring and Test Instruments

r.x: All inspection, measuring and test instruments selected are used to provide the precision required for the inspection process.

The Store Keeper uniquely identifies all instruments and logs in the Equipment Register with the calibration due dates and frequency of calibration. Calibration certificates of all measuring & test instruments used at site will be provided to the MC prior to use & expiry of validity.
Each instrument is calibrated at predetermined intervals and has identification in order to determine the calibration status.
The interval of calibration changes subject to experience with the specific instrument.
Any instrument that cannot be calibrated further is rendered unusable.
The respective QCE / RDE are responsible to ensure that the calibration status of measuring instruments used at site is valid.

In case of any instrument found to be beyond calibration tolerance, the Store Keeper notifies the QCE / RDE who analyses the previous test results to determine the effect of such deviation on the quality of these tests.
During inspection and testing, calibrated instruments are used in suitable environmental conditions as indicated by the manufacturer.
Handling, preservation and storage of inspection, measuring and test equipment is as per manufacturer's instructions.
The Equipment Register (OXYPRO-MC-FM-12) is updated as and when required and the SSK is responsible to ensure and maintain the valid calibration certificates of all measuring instruments.
All inspections and tests shall be carried out based on the approved Inspection and Test Plans.
The required mock-up inspections shall be submitted for consultants approval where applicable, in order to benchmark the upcoming installations.

For all site installation / T&C inspections, the RDE as applicable, initiates the Work Inspection Request (as per project format) attaching the latest shop drawings, Installation Checklist, all other necessary documents and submit to QCE for internal inspection.
The QCE conducts internal inspections as per latest approved shop drawing and actions as below:
If
the work is found acceptable, the QCE countersigns the WIR, Installation Checklist and forward to DC for uploading in mail.
If the work is found unacceptable, the QCE returns the WIR to the initiator for addressing internal Comments and resubmission for internal inspection.
The DC maintains and updates Work Inspection Request Register (OPEM-WIR-Log) for tracking the submission and receipt of Work Inspection Requests.
The RDE and QCE co-ordinates with the MC and Consultant for physical inspection and approval.

If the WIR is rejected by the Consultant, the QCE co-ordinates with Construction / Testing & Commissioning team as applicable, to address consultant’s comments and ensures resubmission of the rejected WIR.

On a weekly basis, the QCE in co-ordination with the Construction Manager reviews the WIR Register (OPEM-WIR-Log) for installation / Testing and Commissioning as applicable and appropriate measures are taken as required for the resubmission of rejected Work Inspection Requests.
The above inspection process is applicable for the subcontracted works by {{CO}}.

Internal Non-conformance identified at site during project execution (E.g. works / materials not in line with the specification)
Deviations from the specifications / drawings identified at site during project execution shall be categorised as below:
Deviations that can be rectified in a time span of maximum three to five working days.
Deviations that shall take more than five working days for rectification.
For deviations that can be rectified in a time span of three to five working days, Site Observation Report shall be issued by the QA/QC Engineer.
The PD / CM ensures appropriate corrections to close the Site Observation Report
Upon verification of the corrections, the QA/QC Engineer, closes the Site Observation Report
The issuance and close out of the SORs are monitored and controlled using Site Observation Report Register

If the Site Observation Report is not closed within {{Q06}} working days from the date of issuance, or not being discussed and / or agreed the course of action with the QA/QC department, the QA/QC Engineer issues the NC & CAR

Deviations from the specifications / drawings, which cannot be rectified in a time span of five working days during project execution (E.g. Installations not in line with the specification), or if the Site Observation Report is not closed as per clause Ref.5.11.3.6 as above, the QCE issues NC & CAR

The PD / CM takes appropriate corrections to address the Non-Conformance and propose suitable corrective measures to avoid the recurrence of the Non-Conformance in co-ordination with the designated functions and / or with the subcontractor.

The proposed corrective measures are suitably addressed to the designated functions and tradesmen via Tool Box Talks / trainings as applicable and are recorded using Addressing Sheet / Personnel Training Record

If the deviation from specification / drawings is identified for a subcontracted work, the Site Observation Report / NC & CAR as applicable, shall be issued to the respective subcontractor by {{CO}} QCE.
The respective CM ensures the close out of the SOR / NCR as applicable.
The discipline QCE is authorized to sign and close the SOR / NCRs related to the site installations.
All NCRs (internal / external) are logged in the NCR Register (OPEM-NCR-Log) and maintained as per the Project File Index
Non-Conformance issued to {{CO}} by the Engineer / Employer
All the NCRs received by {{CO}} are logged in the NCR Register (OPEM-NCR-Log).

The PD / CM takes appropriate corrections to address the Non-Conformance and propose suitable corrective measures to avoid the recurrence of the Non-Conformance in co-ordination with the designated functions and / or with the subcontractor.
The NCR attaching the evidences of close out actions shall be submitted to the Employer / Engineer within the stipulated time frame as required by the contract for close outs.

The proposed corrective measures are suitably addressed to the designated functions and tradesmen via Tool Box Talks / trainings as applicable and are recorded using Addressing Sheet / Personnel Training Record
Process Non-Conformance
The Process Non-conformance is issued by the Projects Head on identifying the non-fulfilment of a requirement during scheduled audits or spot checks.

The respective HOD / PD as applicable, completes the Non-conformance Report identifying the root cause and proposes the corrections, corrective measures specifying the target date for the completion of action items and returns the original to the Projects Head or authorized representative.
The Projects Head / authorized representative verifies the completion of the committed actions and close the Non-Conformance Report.
The Projects Head / authorized representative maintains the log of all Process Non Conformance using NCR Register (OPEM-NCR-Log).
Classification of Audit Findings
As per {{CO}} QMS, the audit findings are categorised as below:
Noteworthy efforts,
Observation / Potential Non-conformance
Non-Conformance

*Note: NCR can be categorised as major / minor depending on the impact, the identified deviation can cause on the QMS performance. As per {{CO}} QMS, this categorisation is not being followed. All deviations from the requirements are given equal importance and addressed accordingly.
Duration for the close out of NCRs

Upon issuing a Non Conformance Report after the internal audit, a maximum of {{Q06}} working days is set as per {{CO}} QMS, to respond to the NCR with the Root Cause Analysis, Corrections, Corrective Actions and the related target dates for close outs. The set target dates for close out shall depend on the nature / type of the NCR.

The NCRs received by {{CO}} from Engineer / Employer will undergo the same process as detailed above. The stipulated time for responding to the NCR shall comply with the Contractual Terms & Conditions.
Confirmation of verbal Instruction (CVI)
All verbal instructions shall be confirmed to the Consultant in writing through MC using the Confirmation of Verbal Instruction (CVI) within the stipulated time as specified in the contract.
The PD / QS jointly assess all the CVIs for time or cost implication if any.
Where the CVIs constitute time or cost implication, it will be treated as variation and a variation claim will be submitted officially to MC.
Where the CVIs affect the subcontractors / suppliers, the CVIs are forwarded to the concerned party for their information and Engineering clarifications if any.
CVIs raised are logged and monitored for confirmation using CVI Register and are maintained in accordance with the Project File Index.
CVIs which constitute Time & Cost Impact are logged in the Variation Register (OPEM-Variation-Log).
The Variation Register (OPEM-Variation-Log) is maintained and updated to monitor the submission and status of Variation Claims.
Request for Information (RFI)
The RDE / DE initiates a Request for Information (RFI) in the following situations:
Requires clarification on a technical document, scope, specifications, drawings or data.
Find conflict, ambiguity, error or omission in or among the technical documents/drawings.
The PD / TD reviews the RFIs and ensures that the request is valid and appropriate before submitting the same to the Main Contractor / Consultant.
RFI Register (OPEM-RFI-Log) is established and maintained to monitor the status of RFI clarifications.
The PD / discipline Engineer follow up with the Main Contractor/Consultant to obtain timely response for the RFIs.
All documents are maintained in accordance with the Project File Index.
Engineers’ Instruction
On receipt of an Engineer’s Instruction, the HO – DC populates the section assigned to be filled by the Document Controller in the Change Control Register
The discipline Design Engineer populates the relevant fields of the Change Control Register and ensures the following:
RFIs are raised as applicable if there is an incomplete / ambiguous information. Refer Clause 5.12 (Request for Information).
The Design Engineer to verify if there is a new technical submittal / revision of the existing submittal has to be made based on the changes; if yes, follow Technical Submittal Review Procedure
If the scope of work assigned to the Subcontractors are affected, co-ordinate with Procurement to forward Enquiry and / or to obtain quote for additional scope.
The Design Engineer ensures that the impact of an Engineer’s Instruction (EI) is communicated to the project team within seven days of receipt of the document by {{CO}}.

Weekly twice, the HO - DC shall distribute the updated Change Control Register (OXYPRO-ED-FM-10) to the PD, CM, Lead Engineers, QS, Planner and DC, with a copy to Director of Projects, Technical Director and Planning Manager.
The PD in co-ordination with the QS, QA/QC, Planner, RDE & CM to check and fill the fields of Change Control Register as applicable.
If abortive / dismantling works are applicable:
QA /QC will be advised to raise Work Inspection Request attaching the photographs for the affected area prior to the start of further works.
The CM to issue the Change Request Form, approved by PD to the foreman to execute the abortive / dismantling works at site.
The project based Lead Engineer to check if the long lead items are affected and to be re-ordered.
If there is an impact on cost and time, due to the abortive works, Variation Procedure to follow.
The QS & the Planner updates the relevant sections of the Variation Register (OPEM-Variation-Log).
The PD or his authorized representative at the project, closes a particular entry in the Change Control Register on completing all subsequent actions pertaining to that specific entry.
Procedure for executing re-works at site

The Discipline Engineer / Construction Manager shall initiate the Change Request Form detailing the description of the changes required, reason for the changes, change category, alternatives considered, technical changes required to implement the change and the associated risks.
The Site DC maintains and updates the Change Request Register
The CM and the QS jointly agree on the estimated cost and the resources required to execute the changes, input the data in the appropriate fields and submit to PD for approval.
Upon PD’s approval of the Change Request Form the DC distributes the original to QS with a copy to CM, Planner, QA/QC, discipline Engineer & foreman.
If the requested changes are due to variations:
The QS to update the Variation Register and Variation Procedure to follow.
The CM to ensure that QA/QC raises Work Inspection Request for the affected works attaching the photographs of the affected area before commencing with any rework.
If the requested changes are not due to Variations, QS to update the details of the work in the Log for abortive works.
The PD / authorized representative to updates the Project Opportunities & Risk Register and the Lessons Learned

If PD rejects the Change Request the PD shall ensure that the suitable actions as recommended is cascaded to all levels of the Project Management including the updating of Project Risk Register and the Lessons Learned.
All instructions received from MC are assessed for any time and/or cost implication.
In case, the instruction constitutes time and/or cost implication, PD notifies MC with a variation notification immediately, in accordance with the contract agreement.

Following the confirmation of {{CO}}’s variation notification by MC, the PD co-ordinates with QS & Planner and issues variation claims substantiated with relevant technical and commercial details, in accordance with the stipulated time required by the contract.
The PD follows up with the MC for the approval of variation works or for the instruction to proceed with the additional works.
QS Logs all variation notifications in the Variation register and monitors the progress of claim submissions and approvals.

Induction for the Project Quality Plan
All project based staff, including the subcontractors are inducted on the Project Quality Plan and induction records are maintained.
The Projects Head/ authorised representatives conduct periodic internal audits / surveillance visits to ensure compliance with the approved Project Quality Plan.
NC and CAR will be issued to the PD for deviations identified to ensure necessary corrections and corrective measures by the concerned functions of the project.
Internal Audit
The Projects Head schedules and control the Internal Audit using Internal Audit Schedule.
The audits shall be planned, taking into consideration the status and importance of the processes and areas to be audited as well as the results of the previous audits.
As a minimum, every project is audited at least twice a year.

Based on the audit schedule, the Projects Head shall nominate the Auditor for each planned audit. Selected auditors perform the role of Technical Experts. While selecting the auditors, the main criteria will be the auditors’ competence in the related field. The auditor shall not audit his own work.
The Projects Head agrees the date and time of the audit with the auditee and issues the Audit Plan, specifying the audit date, audit time, duration, audit purpose, scope, criteria and audit elements.
On completion of the audit, the audit findings shall be explained to the auditee; and the audit report shall be issued.
The findings shall be categorised into 3 types.
1. Noteworthy Efforts, 2. Observations & 3. NCRs.
The NC & CAR shall be issued to the auditee representative.
The Auditee (HOD / Process Owner) proposes the necessary corrections & corrective actions with the target dates, signs the NC & CAR and returns the original NC & CAR to the Compliance Department.
On satisfactory completion of the proposed actions, the Projects Head signs the NC & CAR as ‘CLOSED’ and updates the NCR Register.
Subcontractors’ Audit

The Subcontractor’s audit will be scheduled and managed by the Projects Head in co-ordination with the project team. The Project QA/QC Engineer shall be responsible for ensuring the close out of Audit findings. Only the major Subcontractors fall under the scope of Audit.
Trainings

The performance of an Employee is closely monitored; where gaps are identified internal / external trainings are organised. The respective HOD / Functional Head is responsible for the training need identification and necessary co-ordination with HRD to arrange the trainings.
The competence and development of tradesmen are monitored using skills set chart which is updated at regular intervals.
The Internal trainings / lessons learned workshops are conducted by authorised functions to ensure similar issues are not repeated.

Tool Box Talks are conducted to ensure that the corrective measures taken are cascaded to all relevant functions including the Subcontractors. Evidences related to Tool Box talks, Trainings are maintained.
Management Review
The Management Review meeting shall be conducted at least
once annually
to ensure the continuing suitability of the QMS, adequacy and alignment with the strategic direction of the organization.
Documented information from Management Review shall be maintained.
Management Review Inputs
The management review shall be planned and carried out taking into consideration:
The status of actions from previous management reviews
Changes in external and internal issues that are relevant to the QMS
Information on the performance and effectiveness of the QMS including trends in:
Customer satisfaction and feedback from relevant interested parties
The extent to which quality objectives have been met
Process performance and conformity of products and services
Nonconformities and corrective actions
Monitoring & Measurement Results
Audit Results
The performance of external providers (Suppliers, Subcontractors and Specialists)
The adequacy of resources
The effectiveness of actions taken to address the risks and opportunities
Opportunities for improvement
Management Review Outputs
The outputs of the Management Review shall include decisions and actions related to:
Opportunities for improvement;
Any need for changes to the quality management system;
Resource needs.
The Projects Head prepares and distributes the Minutes of the Meeting as evidence of the results of management reviews.
The Projects Head / authorised representative ensures close out of the respective action items by the responsible functions.
The PD plans and controls the project close out and ensures the following.
Certificate stating that all areas within the project are completed and inspected in accordance with the requirements of the contract.
All inspection, testing and commissioning documents are duly authorised by the appropriate agencies. (i.e. Consultant, local authorities as applicable)
All As Built drawings are submitted
The Operation and Maintenance Manual is compiled and submitted as required by the contract.

If preventive maintenance is part of the project specification, a maintenance schedule for the Equipment which are installed, tested and commissioned shall be developed and maintained, documents of the same will be retained.
Final handing over training for MEP systems are given to Client / Maintenance team.
Defects liability period is agreed.
Final Account is submitted.
Obtain the Certificate of acceptance from the Consultant through MC.
Issue all guarantees for the subcontract works to the satisfaction of MC, Consultants and Authorities.
